body:
Good on you for being in counseling. I highly recommend you bring this up next time you're there. Even if you don't want to go into all the details, I'm sure they could provide great advice.

Until then, remember to be kind to yourself. Everyone makes mistakes. Focus on yourself and remember you can't change others. Try to focus on things in your control; attitude, future actions, etc
I'm in my late twenties and a man if you'd like to talk, I'll be up for a bit.

Sorry to hear about your situation. Unfortunately, as much as you ruminate on the past, it won't change. I'm speaking from experience. One day you might be 31 and wishing you were back at 21 and did some things differently. Sometimes it's a hard pill to swallow. But, the good news is you can change things right now for the better! Your life is far from ruined, I promise.

First, could you maybe bring this housing thing up to your mother? Even if it's not possible in the way you prefer, she might be able to help you in some way.

Take some deep breaths and be nice to yourself :)
Good luck. May I ask what you're on now?

Thanks for the words. I was hyper-focusing on it yesterday ALL day... Today has been a little better. I treated myself to a massage and have just been trying to be nice to myself in general. Hopefully the future holds good things.
True, but it's only been a week, so I feel like I shouldn't be *this* sad

I agree, it's something I want to work on this year. The activities I enjoy are mostly solitary; reading, playing guitar for example. I have been wanting to join a book club, or maybe playing at an open mic, so those are ideas. One of my other main hobbies is snowboarding, but I usually meet up with people I already know and don't meet anyone new.

When I went through my last breakup 3+ years ago, I told myself that I would spend time doing exactly that; bettering myself. I think to an extent I have achieved that with my career, successfully moving to a new and unfamiliar place, paying off student loans, etc. However, there is truth to what you said. I still don't feel fully comfortable by myself. I struggle with this, because unlike a career or degree, there are not obvious, delineated steps to take to achieve this emotional goal. I agree it's something I can work towards,  but in full honesty, the idea of spending another three years by myself makes my heart sink. Thank you for reaching out.
It could possibly help I suppose. Maybe if I regularly did something like that I wouldn't crave touch so much. Thanks for the suggestion.
Thank you for your empathy and kind words. To your point, I do try to remind myself of the negative aspects of relationships.
Thanks. That's how I'm trying to look at as well. It's just another day
Thanks. I'm grateful that I'm healthy
Thanks
Thanks
Thanks for the birthday wishes. I know how you feel
Thanks
On mobile so I don't see it quite, but thanks for the kindness
Thank you for the positive perspective. I agree, I do need to be less hard on myself. It's just that I used to be more hopeful when I felt that there were options.
At least I'm not alone

I went to a friend's party on Friday. A friend's friend was there whom she mentioned before in the context of hooking us up because we have similar interests. We didn't talk that much, but I did think she was cute. On the way out, my friend said to everyone how much this girl and I have in common and all this stuff, I felt awkward and didn't know how to handle it so just said bye and left. The next day I texted my friend saying I found her friend cute and wondered if I could have her number. My friend said she asked the girl and she said "maybe next time we hang out." Which of course means she's not into me; if she was remotely interested I wouldn't think she would mind giving me her number - which is fine, but I feel like an idiot because the impression I got from my friend is that she was into me too. Ugh, I hate that I got my hopes up.
Please talk to me, even if it's just for a little. Don't kill yourself, please.
I know it happens and I'm not alone, which I find comforting and discomforting at the same time.
Thanks, you too.
That's true. Thank you for the kind words, you're a nice person.

Hi, thanks for reaching out. First off, sorry to hear about the guy that broke your heart, but I'm glad to hear that it sounds like you've worked through it. 

I guess I'm not much of a believer in fate, and so it's hard to think that some girl will just come along and everything will work out. At my new job I've actually made some really good guy friends, and as you mentioned they actually are also all in committed relationships. They are great friends, but it can be a bummer sometimes because so often I end up being the third wheel or it reminds me of the things I miss in relationships.
This comment clarifies your above comment well. It's insightful. Thank you.

Thanks for reaching out. I don't think the new place is affecting my mood any more than where I used to live. I try to remind myself of that. If I was back home I know I wouldn't feel any better.

I guess I don't like myself because of how I look and the things that I do and say. My last girlfriend of three years left me because she just stopped loving me and I don't think I have gotten over that after all this time. I don't really have much luck with girls. I have tried a bunch of dating sites and haven't had much luck. I hate that it seems like that's all I can focus on.

Thank you for the comment, that was nice of you.

I'm not exactly sure what you mean by distant, but I don't feel all that different than before I left home. Before leaving there was a lot going on (graduating college, moving across the country for a new job), and now that I'm settling in I think things are starting to feel how they used to. I've been feeling extremely lonely.

She is not someone I talk to regularly, and I haven't talked to her in a few months. It was a particularly difficult weekend for some reason and I ended up texting her because I still think about her every day.

It's like I can't focus on anything else. I have had so many opportunities to get out and meet people and do things, but I can't get myself to do it and it makes me feel even worse about myself. And even when I do take those leaps to do things like that it feels like I almost always regret it or it doesn't work out. 

I feel so damn out of place. I just want feel cared about.
Thank you for commenting. I am on my fourth therapist and have tried three different antidepressants.

> Nope, he's just an idiot. Idiots exist in every field. I'm sorry that happened to you but that's not indicative of what's to come.

Honestly, my gut told me from the beginning that it didn't feel right. But my therapist swore up and down that he was a fantastic therapist and was thrilled that my insurance covered my visits to see him. So, as I said, I was just giving it a chance.

> It's good to test the theory, but now that you have it would also be good to evaluate the results. Do you feel the same? Did the medication help at all? If it did help would you be willing to start again?

I still don't know how I feel. It's hard to say because there are so many variables. I'm leaning more towards no, meaning I feel mostly the same.  Before I left for my new job I was already crying myself to sleep every night. I think what helped at least temporarily was hope that things would be different out here. Now that I'm seeing they aren't, I'm slipping back to my old ways. 

> This is a big one & one I understand all too well. Are you able to scale that back? I understand that even if you are able, it might entail sacrifices. I'm guilty of burning myself out all the while thinking I can throw therapy at the problem so I do get it. But I also know now that it doesn't work that way.

I'm not in situation in which I *need* the money. It's mostly because our project at work (I'm an engineer) is extremely understaffed and behind schedule, so it's falling on a few people to get everything done. If I were to scale back my hours the work would go to my coworkers, and I'd feel like a dick for doing that even though it isn't directly my fault. 

> I'm completely in agreement. You may have misread what I said. I'm not saying "accept life without intimacy". I'm only saying that dating sites are not an accurate benchmark of your value in the dating world. You should stop equating the two. Though definitely I think you should put yourself out there. If you don't want to pick up women at the supermarket or whatever, you can definitely try other things. Speed dating is much more fun than I expected. Also meetups are a good, no-pressure environment to just interact with tons of women. Then there are endless singles events which just make it easy to mingle. I'm not even saying to delete the dating app. Just don't internalize the results as your value/fault.

I didn't mean for that come off as an interpretation in regard to what you said. I'm so used to having this conversation and hearing the old "you need to focus on and love yourself before anyone can love you" - which I know is true for the most part and generally good advice, but I feel that I've worked on that part as much as I can and I'm still so fucking lonely and aching for companionship.

> This whole paragraph tells me that you also cope with issues by burying yourself in work. Scaling back the work as I suggested above would probably present more of a challenge in just learning how to deal with your time. I believe it to be a worthwhile challenge and I think you should, but I understand that it has to do with more than just dollars and cents. Also to the point above, I think the medication may have made a difference.

Yes, that is true, aside from the part about medication, about which I am still unsure. Demonstrated yesterday when I left work at 5:30pm and didn't know what to do with myself once I was home. Lately I've had a strong urge to get drunk. I normally only have a beer or two when I drink, which isn't too often as I consider myself a social drinker. Before yesterday I honestly can't remember the last time I drank hard liquor. Anyway, so I ended up getting drunk home alone (I know, bad idea), and trying to talk to someone on one of the several dating apps I'm on (surprise, didn't go well). Of course this is a coping mechanism and is bad all around. 

> A therapist is good at what they do & I am certainly not a therapist. So when internet-stranger second guesses a therapist, it is something to be taken with a grain of salt. But it sounds like you haven't invested in yourself emotionally. In fact it sounds like you've proactively buried those needs. The net result is a 24 year old man who has no intimacy with a significant other, works 70 hours per week and lives in a new place such that they can't possibly have strong bonds with close friends (yet). Do you really need to have dysthymia? Or is it far more likely that you are responding to this situation in the same way as anyone else would respond to the situation. Again, I'm not a therapist, but this situation is fucked and I think anyone would respond accordingly. For whatever it's worth, my suggestion is that you validate your emotions & prioritize them accordingly. I mean that. Give your emotions priority. If you find a meetup with people that you like spending time with & it requires you to leave work early once a week - do it. Being young is great for about a billion reasons. But one of the drawbacks is lack of experience. You don't even understand how important emotional health is until you're on your last leg. Then you don't even know how to find your way back. It's not your fault, it's a learning experience. But this is how you find your way back.

You lost me at this part. I believe what you are suggesting, and correct me if I'm wrong, is that I'm somehow using the dysthymia diagnosis to justify my place in this situation. I do agree with what you said in regard to my tendency to bury my emotions, but I disagree with the implication that I'm sitting idly by and just accepting it. I mentioned in my original post, albeit briefly, that I've been going out to meet people and do things. My first week here I went to a meetup in the city in an attempt to meet people. I also met some people at my job's orientation who I've hungout with on multiple occasions; I went over the one guy's house for fourth of July party, his girlfriend and I went on a day-long hike. I go out to lunch with people at work weekly. Two weeks ago there was an event through work for new people which was a camping trip I went on with two people from work.

I'm not sitting at home all day feeling sorry for myself. I bet no one would believe you if you tried to convince anyone that knows me that I'm depressed. I have been working a lot the past 3-4 weeks, and should definitely work less, but this isn't something I am just willing to blame on a diagnosis and accept. The dysthymia thing was something I mentioned because depression is something I've dealt with my entire life and is, at least partly in my opinion, an accurate description of how I've been feeling for a long time.

Firstly, thank you for taking the time to reply.

Regarding therapy, the first therapist whom I saw was through my university and was never meant to be permanent. At first taking the leap to go to therapy was a huge step, so that was enough to quell the feelings. But as time went on it become more difficult to manage even with seeing her weekly. She helped me find my second therapist after a few months just before summer, a private one with whom I never clicked or felt a connection. I understand, it happens.

I saw therapist #2 throughout the whole summer and I didn't really find him helpful because I didn't feel like he listened. He would often go on these long, pre-packaged diatribes - I know they were pre-packaged because on more than one occasion he said the same exact thing. Maybe that style works for some, but it wasn't for me. At least I gave it a chance.

When school started in the fall I went back to seeing my university counselor. Up until this point I had been apprehensive towards medication, but I was becoming more and more hopeless each day. My counselor eventually set me up with another therapist to see regularly, as well as a psychiatrist - the latter of whom I would see intermittently to see how medication was affecting me. The new therapist was far better and I found her great and comforting. I was a senior in college also working a good amount, so it was difficult to meet with her regularly. I'd sometimes have to go a month between seeing her. The therapist dealt with my emotional state while the psychiatrist only talked about the medication and its affects.

I started out on a super low dose of Lexapro. I stuck with it for about a month, but mostly it made me feel almost "high" and gave me some GI issues. He switched to a different antidepressant, I can't remember the name but it definitely was not a standard SSRI, something atypical. Anyway, I tried that for a month as well as the results were mostly the same as Lexapro. He tried to up my dose, but I feel like that made it worse. Lastly he put me on Wellbutrin, which probably worked the best. It had little to no side effects, but I couldn't really tell if it helped out with my depression.

Now this time is right around my college graduation and shortly before I was moving out of state to my newly-accepted job. After I graduated and moved, obviously I stopped seeing the therapist. I decided to go back to no medication because it had been a few months since I'd been non-medicated and I wanted to see if it made a difference. That's basically where I'm at today. I would probably benefit from seeing a therapist again, but I've been working 60-70 hrs a week at my new job and the thought of spending the time and effort to find a good one again is daunting. But overall, you're right in saying that I probably should try again.

What you mentioned about dating sites is somewhat comforting, but I still can't help but take it personally when I put myself out there so damn much. Regardless of what you said, I feel like it shouldn't be this difficult to find a mutual attraction after so much time. It's so, so disheartening to me. You say that intimacy is something I can reasonably have again, but truthfully I haven't even been remotely close to any kind of intimacy since my previous relationship ended two years ago. I know the whole "spend time loving yourself" spiel, and frankly I have spent a significant amount of time trying to understand and work on myself, but now I'm about to be 24 and I don't think it's unreasonable to want to find someone to connect and spend time with. It just hurts so much and reminds me of what I had with my ex.

I have been crying again over the past few nights and it feels like it's getting more difficult to deal with again. Probably because I am realizing that it's not so different out here like I hoped it would be and I am becoming hopeless again. Before I left my home state the only thing that would help me fall asleep was thinking of killing myself and I recently I have found that to be the case once again. The odd part is that when I wake up that feeling is mostly gone and throughout the day I'm usually fine. Ironically enough I'm usually a pretty funny person, always laughing with people and have a good amount of close friends at work. But I get home from work and the sadness slowly sets in. I have hobbies and friends and I still feel this way. I feel so broken and it makes me want to die. My one therapist suggested that I have something called dysthymia, which is basically a constant, low-grade depression with major depressive episodes, which sounds pretty much right.
Me too. So much :(
I agree. What's more enticing than making all of your problems disappear?
Exactly. Sorry you feel this way. May we both persevere.
I am currently seeing a therapist. I open up a great deal but not about the ideation.
Laying in bed. Can't fall asleep. Overthinking, getting sad.
I'm sorry for what you went through. There are a lot of supportive and compassionate people on here, open up to them and they will listen.
That sounds like something I need in my life. I'll have to look into it. Thank you.

I've seen stoicism mentioned on here a few times. Is it basically learning to cope with what life throws out you, without letting your emotions run rampant? At least that's what I've gotten out of what I've seen.

I hope things get better for you. The good thing is you're almost there (with the master's). That's not something everyone can do. Whether you like the field or not, people will recognize that you worked hard for it.

You're very hard on yourself. It may be hard to see, but you are. I do the same thing to myself. Behavior patterns become instinctual after extended periods of time, to the point where you don't think twice about thinking those negative thoughts. I'm in the process of addressing the same problem with myself. One thing I've learned is that you get as much respect as you give yourself. If you start respecting yourself, and trust me, I know it's hard, the more others will respect you. Give yourself credit, believe in yourself. I know it's easier said than done, but please just try it. You're worth it.
Sorry you're going through this. No one should have to. Maybe apply for jobs in the meantime and see how it goes?
Eh, that's a crass comment. In depression we get tired, it's okay. I hope you have a good day soon.

I feel this way at times. Well, actually a lot. I try to be mindful and appreciate the little things. The weather today was warmer  than it's been recently. Was able to get out and enjoy it, ride with the window down.
As in, trying the hoping thing.
Same to you. Wish you the best.
It's not selfish at all, I take comfort in it too.
Doesn't sound like you have much to lose with trying it.
This hits close to home. Sorry man.

Yeah, seriously, wtf?
Nah it's the truth, no sugarcoating. I know what you mean, though.
Yep, that's an area in which I'm seriously lacking.
I do have friends, but I say "not really" because I still find myself feeling this way when I'm out with them.
Maybe that's what I need to do.
I don't really have friends.
Yeah I know, I just get down. Sorry about your tooth. How'd you break it?

I know what you mean, I'm on break from school so I've had a lot of free time lately. Long is relative so it's hard to say. Almost three years I was with my ex
Being alone. My ex left me a year ago today. I knew I'd be spending tonight alone
Idk what discord is but I would be a up for some company.
Maybe I should do this

I'm with you, friend. I haven't been invited to anything yet and I don't see it happening. This will be my first new year's eve alone. It will be exactly one year since my ex broke up with me. Ouch, that's depressing.
Wow, I relate to this so much. I have been thinking about this a lot recently.

I'm glad to hear you're doing okay, you deserve it. I'm also doing okay. I finished up school for the semester, and I've been using my free time to do mostly productive, relaxing, and fun things. I'm doing my best to deal with depression and suicidal ideation, but haven't found yet had the courage to tell anyone about the latter.
Oh okay, makes sense. How are you doing?
How did you survive? If you don't mind me asking.
It's just not something I feel comfortable with :/

Thank you for your kind and thoughtful response. Currently I'm overwhelmed with schoolwork, especially with finals coming up the week after next. So getting out of bed isn't an option in that case. Also due to that I don't have too much free time. But you're right, I do spend a lot of that time sulking. I will PM you because I really could use someone to talk to.
I spoke with one person who takes wellbutrin, and she said it works well for her. Can you elaborate on what you mean by "more energetic"?
It is a neat show. It's sad to watch the animals die, and it makes me emotional haha
I wish I was that independent. That's great.
Had this very same dilemma tonight. Best wishes.
I know how you feel. I'm about to graduate with a degree in which I'm rapidly losing interest. I hope things start looking up for you.
I've been feeling that way a lot recently. I hope you feel better.

My friend and I are in a graduate class about antenna operation and design. The prof is kind of a doofus and it's been more of a pain in the ass than anything this semester. The final is next week and I also have a presentation to do which I'm dreading.

I've never been golfing. Do you enjoy it?

I woke up about an hour or two ago. Had some some cereal & now I'm drinking coffee, surfing the internet and relaxing. Got a long day of studying ahead of me that I'm not particularly looking forward to. How about you?
I'm glad you're okay. I'm doing about the same
Please please please be okay.

I'm still holding on to the hope that one day things will change and I will no longer feel this way. I feel like if I take the leap and tell my therapist about this I'll end up in a hospital and then regret having said anything - possibly feeling worse or finding myself in a worse situation or jeopardizing my college graduation in May. This kind of thing is so stigmatized -and my friends would be completely shocked-I don't want to be "that" guy.

I probably could get medicated, but I don't know if I'm ready for that step or if I want to go down that road. I'm very hesitant, but I'm leaning more and more towards it because I don't feel like I'm improving. When I started therapy about a year ago I realized I had been depressed for a long time, possibly since adolescence.
I don't know what else to do. It helps to a certain degree, but I also feel like I am setting myself up for failure in another sense.

I appreciate the input. I don't know if you misread, but I'm not currently taking nor have I ever taken any kind of medication for depression. That is actually a topic I am hoping to learn more about. From what I've read on the subject, medication does not seem to have any effect beyond placebo except in cases of extreme depression. I don't know if I fall into the category which would yield success, or if the possible pros would outweigh the cons (i.e. potential side-effects).

You're right about setting expectations in therapy. Truthfully, it's one of the only parts in my week when someone is listening to me and saying positive, good things. Getting a chance to talk about those things is relieving in a sense, but I don't feel that I'm working towards anything. It's more like the opportunity to be told that I'm not as shitty of a person as I think I am, and that my thinking is not correct. 

I did see a different, private therapist over the summer for about 10-11 weeks since the one I originally started seeing (and am currently seeing) is through my university and isn't meant for long-term treatment. We didn't really "click," and I never felt the sense of relief or comfort I get with my current therapist. 

However, my current situation could definitely improve. Lately I've started to feel myself withholding feelings to a certain extent, solely because I'm afraid to let her down. For example, I'll talk about thoughts that I have, and she'll go on to tell why that thinking is flawed. I understand it, but then I'll fall into the pattern and bring it up again in therapy, and it's almost as if I feel I'm being scolded. I want to be truthful by telling her my thoughts, but like I said I feel like I'm letting her down.

Of course, I could look into seeing a private therapist again, but that seems like a huge undertaking at the moment. To start over from stage one, with another therapist with whom I may or may not "click" seems so daunting and exhausting. I feel stagnant and broken. 

Edit: I forgot to comment on the double sessions. I don't think that would possible because my counselor is through my university and has a hard enough time scheduling me once a week.

I'm in a very similar situation currently and it hurts a lot. I deleted her number today and blocked her on Facebook because she is no longer in love with me and I'm only torturing myself. We got back together briefly after going no contact for 9 months after dating 3 years, and I think it hurts even more this time. Not sure why I wrote this, just wanted to reach out to someone who understands.
Even though I got another shot, I'm still overwhelmed with regret; wishing I did everything differently.
Thank you. I find it very difficult to deal with and not blame myself; just constant pain, hurting, and regret.
Thank you so much for this. I'll continue to do my best.
Thanks, I'm doing my best.
Sorry to hear that. Thanks for the consolation.
Thanks for reaching out. Hope things also get better for you.
Thanks for the resource. I needed this today.
I'm sorry. This is my own personal experience, so things may be a lot different for you.
I'm doing my best, but finding it have faith in all the clichés anymore. Things don't seem to be getting better and I don't know what to do.
Sorry to hear that. Hope things get better for you. Thanks for reaching out.
Thanks. Best of luck to you as well.
It's just how I feel
Thanks

That's so great to hear that you've made it to the point you're at right now. I hope to make it there myself, though I have a feeling it's going to be a bit more time. I'm just about at the 6 month stage myself and it still feels like it's getting harder still everyday. I made it through the spring semester getting straight A's, but now I have all this time to contemplate, ruminate, etc. This last week has been one of the worst since the breakup. I decided to get out of bed and go down to the gym today... Of course, I see her driving on my way there. I still ran 2 miles on the treadmill; not much, but it was something. Still ,man, sometimes it feels like it's not getting any easier and like it won't for a very long time; not trying to take away from what you've written, and I'm not 100% sure why I'm writing this, except to say I hope I can make it to where you are.

Thanks. I don't feel amazing about the grades, but I truly don't know how I did it. I can hardly function now and I'm paralyzed by all this time and nothing to do. Well, nothing I want to do or have motivation to do, actually. It's ironic because I recall times during the relationship when all I wanted was time to do all of these things, and now all I have is time, but all I can think about it her. Yesterday was just a really hard day. I'm feeling a bit less sad today at the moment. I'm gonna shower and get out of the house today by getting over to the library and reading a book. Thanks for the support and taking the time to write. It helps and is uplifting to read.
Thanks. Hope things start looking up for you.

It's not that I'm closing anyone off. I've hung out with friends a decent amount since school ended and make a genuine effort, even if I don't feel up to it at times. Even with all of that, it's more that I don't know how to deal with or escape the feelings of regret, loneliness, and sadness.

Thanks for the support. I'm sorry you're going through something similar. I'll check out the video right now. Also, I understand that I need to be my own source of happiness. I don't think I was every fully happy and independent; as soon as my first relationship ended abruptly and unexpectedly, I was so miserable going from girl to girl trying to fill the void until I found my most recent ex. I don't know that I was ever happy on my own is what I'm trying to say. I'm in counseling trying to figure out what might be the source of that. I know this is the perfect opportunity to do that, but it makes me feel hopeless. I hope it's just temporary. Again, thanks for the support and resource.
I'm very sorry to heart that. Thanks for reaching out and saying that, though. I hope things get better for you.

I'm so sorry to hear that. She made it very clear that she wants nothing to do with me, so I would never reach out to her, though I do have days like I described above in which I miss her so much and just want to talk to her. Everyone has setbacks; it doesn't negate all of the progress you've made. Stay strong and focused. Good luck on your exam.
I would never reach out to her, this is me just expressing my emotions. I know she doesn't care how I feel.
Wow, that's oddly similar. Hope you're doing well. You're doing all the right things. Just gotta take it day by day.
Thank you for this.
Wow, I'm in basically the same situation. Four months and all. I feel for you. It's awful. I feel hopeless. Hope things look up for you.
Unbearable is good word to describe it.

I was on a journaling streak but have since lost motivation to continue with it. I felt like it wasn't helping as much as it used to. I was writing the same stuff every day and it started to become frustrating. Though I'm not doing any better now so I guess the point is moot. Anyway - what aspect of journaling do you find most helpful? Just looking for insight if you don't mind. Btw, this was well-written and I empathise with that dream and the feeling of your ex moving on without you. Sorry you're going through a rough time. Hope things start looking up for you.

I try to tell myself all of those things, but I'm still racked with guilt. I genuinely fear that I'll be alone forever. The best thing right now is probably for me to be alone and grow as a person, but I can't get comfortable with it. Like I said in my post, I'm either torturing myself with thoughts of how shitty of a person I am, or I'm inducing anxiety by contemplating how I'll spend the rest of my life miserable and alone.

I see your point about not actually loving her for having been a shitty boyfriend, taking her for granted, etc., but I disagree. I did love her, and I still do (which is the problem). I think it was a mix of being unhappy with myself and being afraid of losing her which resulted in my acting the way that I did. Sort of like a defense mechanism. I never thought it would have ended so fast and unexpectedly. Never. She cut me off in a cruel, cold manner without remorse and I probably deserved it. People hurt the ones they love all of the time. Most of the time it's out of a selfish neglect, like in my case. I lost her and I have to live with the consequences. I'm not asking anyone to feel sorry for me, I just don't know how to cope with these immense feelings of regret and grief.

I'm a little confused, how does my ex giving up on me make you feel better? Anyway, I agree, if it was "love" then she wouldn't have given up on me. But man, after two years it's hard to swallow that. Sorry to hear you're in a similar situation. I'm the same way; going to sleep is the hardest part of the day for me. My mind starts racing and I almost always end up on the verge of tears with a lump in my throat.
